source.title: Free Gait Analysis | Summit Run Shop

variants.control:
Free Gait Analysis | Summit Run Shop
Free Gait Analysis At Summit Run Shop, every visit includes a free gait analysis. We watch you walk and run, check your arch height and ankle mobility, and look at how far your foot rolls inward as it lands. Runners who overpronate often do well in a stability shoe with a firmer medial post, while neutral runners usually prefer more flexible cushioning. Bring the socks you run in and, if you use them, your orthotics, so the fit matches how you actually run.

source.title: How to Choose Your First Marathon Shoe | The Long Run

variants.control:
How to Choose Your First Marathon Shoe | The Long Run
How to Choose Your First Marathon Shoe Your first marathon block will put more miles on your legs than anything you have done before, so the shoe matters. Prioritise comfort over speed: the lightest racing shoe is tempting, but most of your training happens at an easy pace, where cushioning and a secure fit do more for you than a carbon plate. Try shoes on late in the day, when your feet are at their largest, and leave a thumb's width of space at the toe.

source.title: Common Running Injuries and How to Prevent Them | Front Range Physio

variants.control:
Common Running Injuries and How to Prevent Them | Front Range Physio
Common Running Injuries Shin splints, runner's knee, plantar fasciitis and Achilles tendinopathy account for most of the running injuries we treat. The most common cause is doing too much too soon: increasing weekly mileage faster than tendons and bones can adapt. Build volume gradually, keep at least one easy day between hard sessions, and add two short strength sessions a week for your calves, hips and core. If pain changes the way you run, stop and get it assessed.

source.title: Aerofoot Expands Shoe Recycling Program to 200 Stores | Gear Wire

variants.control:
Aerofoot Expands Shoe Recycling Program to 200 Stores | Gear Wire
Aerofoot Expands Shoe Recycling Program Runners can now drop off worn-out athletic shoes of any brand at 200 Aerofoot stores, the company said on Tuesday. Collected shoes are ground into rubber granules for playground surfaces and running tracks. The program, which began as a pilot in three cities last year, has collected more than 400,000 pairs. Aerofoot said it plans to add drop-off bins at partner retailers next spring.
